column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health
Ship the run manifest and serve the app on the port and health path stated in Deployment.

Accounts and sessions
Seeded and invited people sign in with email and password, followers create their own public account (also from the sign-in screen without losing the page they came from), and every signed-in account can read its own profile, as stated in API.

One error shape and precedence
Every API error uses the single error shape and the single precedence order stated in API.

Same-origin requests and size limits
The server refuses cross-origin writes, oversize bodies and unsupported content types, and never serves source files or credentials, as stated in Server boundary.

Boot with a dependency down
The app starts and answers health while storage, mail or billing is unreachable, reports the outage honestly on each affected action, and recovers without a restart once the service returns.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment variables named in Configuration and secrets, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.

Responsive layout at the published widths
Every screen switches layout at exactly the widths in the Screens and layout table and fits the three viewports with no horizontal page overflow.

Keyboard-complete flows and tap targets
Every journey completes by keyboard alone in reading order with a visible focus ring, every dialog keeps Tab inside, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener, and every tap target meets the size in Visual design.

Motion rules and reduced motion
Motion follows the timings in Motion and effects, nothing loops for decoration, and the reduced-motion setting swaps each motion for its stated substitute.

Editing-bay look
Every surface sits on the graphite ground with warm off-white ink, and the single amber accent appears only on the playhead and the active selection.

Type and tabular numerals
Headings use the grotesk display face, body text uses the plain sans, and every timecode, count and price is set in the monospaced face with figures that do not shift as digits change.

Frame pluck craft
The strip, playhead, preview and flight to the tray read as one editing-bay tool, and the plucked tile is visibly the same image from strip to slot.

Upload references
Seated designers upload images and clips to their brand wall, only files whose leading bytes are a supported image or clip are accepted, and a reference exists only once its file is stored.

Stored objects match references
Every reference has exactly one stored object and every stored object has exactly one reference, through uploads, plucks, deletions and storage failures.

Seat required for edits
Designers without a pro seat can view their brand workspace, but every change their role otherwise allows is refused with the seat error, as qualified in Business rules.

Brand-scoped literal search
Global search results and counts come only from the current brand workspace, match the typed text literally, and still find a still by its recorded source clip title after the clip is deleted.

Brand-scoped pickers and cursors
The add-to-cluster picker and tray switcher list only the current workspace's clusters, and every listing cursor is refused anywhere other than the workspace and surface that issued it, as stated in Business rules.

Add to cluster with announced count
Adding a reference to a cluster appends it at the end of the tray, rolls the item count and announces the result in the tray live region.

Collect references journey
A designer signs in, uploads references, searches, finds a cluster through the picker, adds items and sees them numbered in the tray after a reload.

Sprocket strip
Opening a clip docks a full-width strip under the wall that never scrolls and samples as many evenly spaced frames as fit its width, at least 8 or every frame when the clip has fewer, with a playhead, a large preview and a timecode readout.

Playhead scrubbing
Dragging the playhead by mouse or touch, or pressing the stated keys, moves through frames in step with pointer position across the strip's full width, a touch drag never scrolls or zooms the page, and the preview and timecode update on every frame step.

Plucked still with timecode
Plucking stores the current frame as a still that keeps its source clip and a timecode computed by the server, and appends it to the end of the active cluster.

Pluck flight and count roll
The plucked tile flies as one element from its place in the strip to its numbered tray slot, and the item count rolls up by one, with the timings in Motion and effects.

Pluck when storage is down
When storage is unreachable the pluck saves nothing, the tile returns to the strip, focus stays on the playhead, the cluster stays usable, and an honest error is shown and announced.

Pluck announcement and focus
Each pluck result, success or failure, is announced in the tray live region with the exact copy from Feedback states and focus ends on the playhead.

Pluck a frame journey
A designer opens an uploaded clip, scrubs to a frame, plucks it into a cluster and after a reload sees the same still, timecode and slot.

Keyboard reorder
A designer lifts a tray item with the keyboard, moves it with the arrow keys, the other items shifting with the timing in Motion and effects, and drops it, focus stays on its handle, and the new order persists.

Drag reorder
Dragging a tray item to a new slot shows the new order at once and saves the same order an equivalent keyboard move would.

Concurrent order changes
Simultaneous adds and plucks each get their own slot with positions staying exactly 1 to n, and of several moves sent against one version exactly one wins while the rest are refused with the latest order, as stated in Business rules.

Reorder announcements and rollback
Each keyboard lift, step, drop, cancel, refusal and conflict is announced with the exact copy from Feedback states, and a refused move is never left on screen.

Cluster sheet export
A cluster exports as a CSV sheet in presentation order that contains only that cluster's entries, with formula-like title and source clip cells neutralised as stated in API.

Order a cluster for presentation journey
A designer reorders a cluster by keyboard and by drag, sees a move refused on a locked cluster roll back, reloads to see the saved order and downloads a sheet in that order.

Review link invite
Creating a review link for a cluster in review emails the link to the freelancer, and nothing is created if the email cannot be sent.

Review link scope
A review link shows exactly one cluster's entries and comments and gives no access to sibling clusters, the wall or any workspace endpoint.

Review link expiry
A review link and the media it serves work until the link's expiry instant, which only the server clock decides to the millisecond, and are refused from that instant on, as stated in Business rules.

Revoke, regenerate and offboard
Revoking a link, regenerating it or offboarding a collaborator kills the affected links and their media access at once, and a regenerated link replaces the old one.

Read-only review links
A link without comment permission can view the cluster, but every write through it is refused.

Freelancer review journey
A freelancer opens the emailed link, reviews the cluster in order and leaves a comment that the designer then sees on the cluster.

Cluster status transitions
Clusters move only along the legal edges of the lifecycle in Business rules, and each illegal edge is refused.

Locked clusters
Embargoed, public and withdrawn clusters refuse changes to their entries, order and privacy flags.

Withdrawal
Only the cluster owner or a design ops lead withdraws a public cluster, and withdrawal removes its public page, profile listing, feed entry and public media at once, except media that another public cluster still holds.

Cluster lifecycle journey
A designer creates a cluster, sends it to review and returns it to draft, and an ops lead withdraws a public cluster and sees it disappear from the public side.

Embargo in brand time
An embargo is set as a local date and time in the brand workspace's time zone and resolves to an instant that stays correct across daylight-saving changes, as qualified in Business rules.

Public from the lift instant
An embargoed cluster is public from its lift instant exactly, on every read and write and on every app instance, whether or not a background job has run, and no screen decides it from the device clock.

Public cluster page
The public cluster page and its API show only the published fields and public items, never internal notes, private items or comments.

Follower digest once per lift
Each follower of the cluster owner receives exactly one digest email per lift, even with several app instances running or mail briefly down.

Digest is exactly four public lines
The digest email is plain text whose body is exactly the four published lines, carrying only public cluster fields and never internal notes, private item titles, comments or other people's details.

Embargo release journey
A designer schedules an embargo, the cluster lifts, the open settings screen shows Public, and a follower sees the public page and finds the digest in their inbox.

Stable discovery feed
The discovery feed serves capped pages, newest first with ties broken by id, that never repeat or skip a cluster while others are published or withdrawn mid-scroll.

Public curator profile
A curator profile shows display name, handle, follower count and public clusters only, and a cluster's credits show display name and handle only.

Follow and follower counts
Following and unfollowing a curator can be repeated or sent simultaneously, and the follower count always equals the number of follows.

Discovery journey
A signed-out visitor on a phone opens the menu, presses Follow on a curator profile, signs up from the sign-in screen, returns to that profile, follows, sees the count update and scrolls the feed.

Invite designers
An ops lead invites a designer by email, the designer accepts through the emailed link, and nothing is created if the email cannot be sent.

Seat roster
An ops lead sees each brand workspace's seat meter and roster and assigns or frees seats within the cap of the active subscription.

Last seat goes to one lead
When two ops leads assign the last seat to different designers at the same moment, exactly one assignment succeeds and the other gets the no-seats-left result.

Seat admin journey
An ops lead invites a designer, assigns them the last seat, sees the meter full and sees the no-seats-left message on the next attempt.

Plan upgrade across billing
An upgrade changes the Kill Bill subscription and the workspace seat cap, and sends the receipt email, all together.

Upgrade replay safety
Retrying an upgrade with the same idempotency key changes nothing and returns the original result, reusing the key for a different plan is refused, and a key still running on any instance is refused as in progress.

Upgrade undone when billing or mail fails
If billing or mail fails during an upgrade, the plan, seat cap and inbox end exactly as they were before, and the lead sees an honest error.

Upgrade the plan journey
An ops lead upgrades a full workspace's plan, sees the new seat meter and the receipt confirmation, and assigns the seat that just opened.

Uploads carry no hidden metadata
Uploaded images and plucked stills are stored and served without the embedded metadata listed under Upload hygiene and with their image data unchanged, and media is served with a fixed type that browsers will not sniff.

Review comments are rate-limited
Comments through review links are capped per freelancer email and cluster across all app instances with an exact retry delay, and a refused comment keeps its text while Post comment waits out that delay, as stated in Business rules and Interactions.

Status changes one at a time
Simultaneous status changes on one cluster are applied one at a time across all app instances, and each later request is judged against the status the earlier one left.

Return only to Rushes
After sign in or sign up, Rushes returns the user to the page they came from only when it is a path inside Rushes, as stated in Business rules.

Latest search text wins
The wall search and the add-to-cluster picker only ever show the answer to the text currently in the field, and a late answer to earlier text is never shown.

Search lives in the address
An active wall search lives in the address as q, so reload, Back and Forward restore the same literal query, results and counts.

Settings refresh keeps unsaved work
The cluster settings screen re-reads the server at least every 30 seconds without discarding unsaved text, closing an open dialog, moving focus to another control or re-enabling a pending control.

Collapsed navigation and tray are unavailable
Below 720 pixels wide the main navigation and the cluster tray collapse behind buttons whose panels open and close in the time stated in Motion and effects, and while collapsed nothing inside them is visible, focusable or exposed to assistive technology.

Seat admin updates in place
Every assign, free and invite answer, including a no-seats-left refusal, updates the seat meter, with its numbers rolling as stated in Motion and effects, and the roster in place from the server's state without navigation, with focus as stated in Interactions.

Plan and cap come from Kill Bill
The plan, seat cap and upgrade choices are what Kill Bill's active subscription reports on every read while it is reachable, including plans changed directly in Kill Bill and caps below the seats in use.

Error summary on refused forms
Every form submit refused with field errors shows a focused error summary above the form that links to each invalid field, with each field marked invalid and described by its exact message.

Explore keeps its pages in the address
The number of Explore pages loaded lives in the address, so reload, Back and Forward load that many pages again, capped at ten even when interactive loading records more.

Roster view lives in the address
The admin roster's seat filter and sort live in the address, so reload, Back and Forward restore the same rows and control values.

Follow responds at once and rolls back honestly
Follow and Unfollow change the button and count at once and, when refused, return visibly to the earlier state with the published copy.

Seat changes respond at once and roll back honestly
Assigning and freeing a seat change the row and meter at once and, when refused, show the server's state with the published copy and no ghost row.

Status actions respond at once and roll back honestly
A status action changes the status label at once and, when refused, shows the server's status or the earlier status with the published copy.

Status never by colour alone
Cluster status labels, review link states, the seat meter state and the current plan marker each carry text and an icon as well as colour.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and no other runner is needed.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package with its licence, plus each bundled font; shipped packages are the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.

Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), including any native library it bundles, and every font uses MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or OFL-1.1.

The app uses no datastore beyond Postgres, MinIO, Kill Bill and Mailpit's SMTP: no SQLite, no Redis, no embedded database, no in-process state shared between requests as a store, and no local files used as storage.
The provided service configuration and seeded environment values are left untouched.
Fonts and scripts are served from the app itself, with no request to a third-party host at runtime.
The application source is TypeScript, and package-lock.json is committed.
